**RE: Urgent Member Appeal for Prior Authorization Denial**
*   **Member Name:** Taylor Alvarez
*   **Member ID:** W709290584
*   **Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield (Commercial/ACA), Indiana
*   **Requested Service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT Code: 63030)
*   **Reference Number:** POC-A43FE266AD-51849
*   **Denial Date:** August 21, 2026
*   **Surgeon:** Dr. Reyes, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)

To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of the prior authorization request for my lower back disc surgery and decompression (CPT 63030), which is scheduled to be performed by Dr. Reyes. 

The denial letter dated August 21, 2026, states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." This determination is incorrect and is directly contradicted by my objective clinical records, which fully satisfy the plan’s governing clinical criteria. 

According to the Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines for Spine Surgery (Doc ID: MSK03-1125.1, Effective November 15, 2025), which Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield applies to CPT 63030, a lumbar decompression is considered medically necessary for an "Initial disc herniation when ALL the following criteria are met." Below, I map my clinical records directly to each of these criteria to demonstrate full medical necessity:

### 1. Imaging Findings and Clinical Correlation
The guideline requires: 
> "Documentation of nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on MRI or other advanced imaging performed within the past 6 months that correlates with clinical findings"

My lumbar spine MRI, performed on **June 9, 2026** (well within the past 6 months), explicitly documents:
*   **L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.**

The guideline also states:
> "If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

My radiologist's report clearly identifies the severe nerve compression. These imaging findings perfectly correlate with my clinical presentation, which features severe radicular pain extending into my right calf, positive provocative testing on the right side, and a corresponding neurological deficit [e.g., diminished sensation or weakness in the right L5 distribution].

### 2. Clinical Presentation and Functional Impairment
The guideline requires:
> "Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as: Nerve root tension sign · Dermatomal sensory loss · Motor strength deficit (myotomal) Abnormal reflex"

My records document severe radiculopathy that meets multiple elements of this criterion:
*   **Significant Functional Impairment:** Due to the severe radiating pain down my right leg, my functional capacity is severely limited. I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes [and my ability to perform basic activities of daily living, such as walking short distances and performing household tasks, is severely disrupted]. My pain level is consistently rated [e.g., 7/10], which exceeds the threshold defined under the guideline's general requirements.
*   **Physical Exam Findings:** Dr. Reyes' physical examination notes positive provocative testing (including a positive straight leg raise/nerve root tension sign) on the right side, along with corresponding dermatomal sensory loss and motor deficits that match the compressed L5 nerve root seen on my MRI.

### 3. Failure of Conservative Management
The guideline requires:
> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management"

My conservative management has far exceeded this minimum requirement:
*   **Physical Therapy:** I completed **12 weeks** of supervised, professional physical therapy from April 4, 2026, to June 27, 2026, totaling 20 completed visits. This therapy focused on lumbar flexibility and core stabilization, but my symptoms progressively worsened. This is fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
*   **Medication:** I tried conservative medical management with NSAIDs for 8 months without adequate relief.
*   **Interventional Therapy:** I received a lumbar corticosteroid injection on April 3, 2026, which provided only 2 weeks of temporary, partial relief before the radicular pain returned to its baseline severity.

### 4. Rule Out of Alternative Pain Sources
The guideline requires:
> "All other reasonable sources of pain have been ruled out"

My clinical history confirms that all other reasonable sources of pain have been ruled out. I am a non-smoker, have a BMI of 29, have no active infections, and have no untreated substance use disorders. There are no competing diagnoses or confounding variables; my pain is entirely generated by the severely compressed L5 nerve root documented on my June 2026 MRI.

### Conclusion

I have suffered from progressive, debilitating lower back and leg pain for 14 months. I have exhausted all conservative treatment pathways, including an extensive 12-week course of physical therapy, oral medications, and an epidural injection, all without lasting relief. My MRI provides undeniable, objective proof of a severe disc extrusion compressing my right L5 nerve root, which directly correlates with my physical symptoms and functional limitations.

Because my clinical records satisfy every medical necessity requirement of the Carelon Spine Surgery Guideline, I request that you immediately reverse this denial and approve the requested lumbar decompression (CPT 63030) so that I can proceed with my scheduled surgery under Dr. Reyes' care.

I have attached my June 9, 2026 MRI report, physical therapy discharge summaries, and clinical notes from Dr. Reyes for your immediate review. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I look forward to your timely response.

Sincerely,

Taylor Alvarez
